messages.subject: array to matrix conversion
messages.body_plain:
Is the transpose() operator slow, or the matrix() operator slow?

I am writing a multi-fleet stock assessment model that has Francis' (2014) compositional likelihood, with correlation in the residuals (reference below). Because the model has multiple gears, and I expect the correlation in sampling error to be different between gears, I'm storing the correlation matrix in a 3D array, i.e.

array<Type> Corr_gll(nG,nL,nL)

where nG = 6 is the number of gears, and nL = 54 is the number of length classes. When i go to recover the correlation matrix I was originally using a transposition and a conversion from array:

matrix<Type> tmpCorr_ll = Corr_gll.transpose().col(g).matrix()

but I found that this really slowed down initialising the ADFun object with makeADFun()

When I removed the transposition and matrix operation, and instead filled the matrix using a loop, things got much faster. Any ideas where the slow down is?

 Francis, R. C. (2014). Replacing the multinomial in stock assessment models: A first step. Fisheries Research, 151:70–84.

messages.subject: Re: array to matrix conversion
messages.body_plain:
"Is the transpose() operator slow, or the matrix() operator slow?"

The array.transpose() is slow because it literally creates a new object regardless of the operations you put after the transpose. This is not Eigen's fault because the implementations of TMB arrays are only partially based on Eigen.
To do constructs like the following for many 'g':

Corr_gll.transpose().col(g).matrix()

one should start by transposing the array once, and put it in a temporary:

tmp = Corr_gll.transpose();
matrix<Type> tmpCorr_ll = tmp.col(g).matrix();

I must admit though, that I'm a bit surprised that an array of dimension (6,54,54) should cause an observable slowdown. I suspect something else is wrong (perhaps you are compiling with '-O0' or perhaps you are repeating the array transpose more times than you think...)

messages.subject: cast from type double to integer
messages.subject_clean: cast from type double to integer
messages.body_plain:
I have a matrix of derived quantities inside my model which do not (explicitly) depend on parameter values.

I would like to round these to the nearest integer, stash that output separately, and use the result to index within a different matrix. I currently have a static, externally-generated lookup table but would like to use the "live" values for accuracy.

So far I have tried:

 int temp_ind = int(matrix_of_doubles(x,y,z));
 return_val = other_table(temp_ind); // must be an integer

And received error: invalid cast from type 'CppAD::AD<double>' to type 'int'. If I substitute a raw double for  matrix_of_doubles(x,y,z)  (e.g. 3.14159) this error doesn't come up. I suspect TMB is thinking that matrix_of_doubles is deeply related to differentiated parameters, and therefore shouldn't be rounded?

For what it's worth, I'm trying to use the predicted lengths-at-age to look up selectivity values associated with that length bin. In my model, the predicted lengths in question are deterministic (no estimation of growth parameters).

Is there a way to store the rounded value of a derived double, with no intention of modifying the original quantity?

Thanks
MK

I've also used Intel VTunes to profile my TMB code on a Windows machine. In the VTunes Configure Analysis Section, I attach the R process using the PID. messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] ARM based macs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sam,

I recently updated to an M1 Mac. I haven’t had time to test timing, OpenMP, etc., but I got it working. In general, I followed the steps described here http://yiqingxu.org/public/BigSurError.pdf

In step 4.1 it should say "gcc --version" but the formatting did something.

In step 5, it’s important to read where it says "Note that “x86_64- apple-darwin20/10.2.0” can be different for you." Mine is "aarch64-apple-darwin20/11.0.0", but yours might be different. Look what’s in "/usr/local/gfortran/lib/gcc/".

I’ll report back when I get into OpenMP, but I would be happy to hear if someone else already did this.

cheers,
Mollie

messages.body_plain:
Hi.
While printing characters on screen using std::out, my machine is sensitive to whether the quotation is single or double.  For example,

(1) std::cout<<"ABC: "<<std::endl;
This results in a compile error.
 vs.
(2) std:cout<<'ABC: '<<std::endl;
This passes compile-link, but the character, "ABC" does not show up on the screen.

I use Windows 10, and my current R info is as follows:
  platform       x86_64-w64-mingw32
  arch           x86_64
  os             mingw32
  system         x86_64, mingw32

  svn rev        80725
  language       R
